prerequisites: Basic knowledge of modeling and setting up system equations
Fundamentals of mechanics and electrical engineering
Basic knowledge in computer science, especially programming
Basic knowledge in mathematics: numerical methods, solving differential equations, series expansion (Taylor, Fourier), matrix calculus
Ability to abstract physical systems and purpose-oriented modeling
Sufficient practice in applying prior knowledge from mathematics and mechanics

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of models and modeling approaches for dynamic/technical systems.
A deeper understanding of methods and procedures in numerical simulation, building on the fundamentals of numerical mathematics, should be conveyed.
Introduction to continuous simulation languages and simulation software should enable the appropriate use of simulation technology.
This also includes knowledge of the methodical approach (modeling, coding, debugging, validation, etc.).

Application of textual simulators (e.g., MATLAB) and graphical simulators (Simulink and others) to solve problems in the field of dynamic/technical systems, preparing for the use of simulation technology in specific subject areas (control engineering, mechatronics, design, multi-body dynamics, fluid mechanics, etc.).
Introduction to special simulation tasks such as real-time simulation, Hardware-in-the-Loop, multi-methods, parallel simulation, simulator coupling (co-simulation).
Overview and presentation of discrete simulation.
Acquisition of the ability for problem- and effort-adapted model building for the treatment of dynamic problems in real machines.
Acquisition of analytical and numerical skills for treating model-motion equations.
Ability to interpret simulated phenomena of dynamic/technical systems.
Basic knowledge of advanced topics in simulation technology.
Communication in solving problems in a team, discussion and presentation of results and proposed solutions.
To concisely describe models and modeling approaches for dynamic/technical systems.
To structuredly present methods and procedures of numerical simulation based on fundamentals of numerical mathematics.
To safely apply continuous simulation languages and simulation software for the appropriate use of simulation technology.
To systematically carry out modeling, coding, debugging, and validation as a methodical procedure.
To reliably use textual and graphical simulators (e.g., MATLAB/Simulink) to solve relevant problems.
To purposefully transfer simulation technology to specific subject areas such as control engineering, mechatronics, design, multi-body dynamics, and fluid mechanics.
To clearly explain the specifics of real-time simulation, Hardware-in-the-Loop, multi-methods, parallel simulation, and co-simulation.
To structuredly present basic principles of discrete simulation.
To formulate models for dynamic problems in real machines in a problem- and effort-adapted manner.
To reliably solve model-motion equations using analytical and numerical methods.
To present complex content, models, and results in an audience-appropriate manner.
To precisely formulate mathematical arguments, notation, and documentation.
To independently and cooperatively plan work processes in simulation projects with regard to time and resources in a structured manner.
To purposefully use digital tools for programming, version control, and documentation.
To clearly formulate team roles, communication channels, and coordination rules in group work processes.
To constructively discuss peer feedback on models, implementations, and evaluations.
To systematically examine data sources, model assumptions, and numerical results for plausibility and consistency.
To compare alternatives of modeling, discretization, and solution strategies based on defined criteria.
To purposefully find relevant scientific sources and software documentation.
To concisely summarize learning progress and key statements from lectures and exercise phases.

syllabus_topics: Models and modeling approaches for dynamic/technical systems
Fundamentals of numerical methods in continuous simulation
Introduction to continuous simulation languages, simulation software
Application of MATLAB/Simulink, among others, to solve problems
Preparation for the use of simulation technology in special subject areas (control engineering, mechatronics, design, etc.)
teaching_methods: Audiovisual lecture with media support over theoretical fundamentals
Practice of learned material by independently solving tasks, partly in teams and under instructor guidance
